# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 56 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 56 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_056_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 5, Part 2 — Hermas Asks for the Interpretation

**56:1** I asked him to explain the parable to me. "What is it that you seek to know?" he said. "Lord," I said, "why is the son's inheritance not enough for the slave? Why does the master set him up as co-heir with the son?"

**56:2** "Listen," he said. "The slave who kept the commandment and the instruction of the master — this one is the sacred spirit who dwelt in the flesh. And his flesh served this spirit well and walked in holiness and purity, in no way defiling the spirit."

**56:3** "When therefore the flesh had so lived well and purely, and had labored together with the spirit and cooperated with it in everything, conducting itself with valor and courage, he chose it as a partner with the sacred spirit. For the conduct of this flesh pleased the Lord, seeing that it was not defiled while bearing the sacred spirit upon the earth."

**56:4** "He took the son and the trustworthy slaves as counselors. These are the sacred angels who were first created. The master took this counsel with them, that this flesh, having served the sacred spirit blamelessly, should have some place of sojourn, lest it should appear to have lost the reward of its service."

**56:5** "For every flesh in which the sacred spirit has dwelt shall receive a reward if it is found undefiled and spotless. You have the interpretation of this parable also."

---

*EMET renders the Greek of P.Mich. 130 with maximal literalness, preserving the adoptionist-tendency christology of Similitude 5's interpretation.*
